story-context.summary: Replace embedded base64 background images in form definitions with reusable asset references. Introduce storage provider abstraction, config-backed limits, and shared resolver parity.
story-context.problem-statement: The builder currently stores background images as Data URLs inside FormVersion.DefinitionJSON, bloating payloads and risking preview/production drift. We need asset-based backgrounds with consistent resolution and storage-backed lifecycle management.

key-features.feature: Asset upload/storage for background images (no base64 in DefinitionJSON)
Storage provider abstraction (Local dev ↔ Azure Blob via config)
Runtime URL generation (no absolute host persisted)
Placement + cropping with intersection auto-remove if off-canvas
Asset lifecycle: dedup by hash, soft-delete, rename
Defensive guard against embedded Data URL backgrounds

reference-documents.document: Epic 5 scope and proposed story roadmap (Story 5.1 foundation)
Epic 5 workflow phases and Git discipline
PRD anchors for preview/testing and publishing (downstream dependency)
Mandatory naming conventions for any new DB objects

key-types.type: Reference stored in the form definition (asset ID/key + placement metadata)
Stored asset metadata (hash, size, mime, storage path, display name)

key-files.file: Replace Data URL background handling with asset references and placement metadata
Asset storage abstraction (Local/Azure) and asset metadata management
Asset upload endpoints and retrieval URLs (tokenized/secure if needed)
DB migration for asset metadata table (human executes migration commands)

done-criteria.criterion: DefinitionJSON stores only asset references (no Data URLs)

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Background images are stored as assets, not embedded in JSON
Runtime URL resolution is shared and consistent
Upload and runtime limits are enforced via config.AppSetting
Off-canvas backgrounds auto-remove from canvas while asset remains in library
Dedup and soft-delete are supported without breaking existing forms
Data URL backgrounds are blocked/stripped with clear errors

forbidden-zones.zone: Do not persist base64 image blobs in FormVersion.DefinitionJSON
Do not hard-code limits (must use config.AppSetting)
Do not couple to a single storage provider

risks.risk: Storage provider abstraction must be correct to avoid production asset access failures.
Asset reference migration/guard paths must prevent Data URL regressions.

metadata.story-title: Background Asset Management (No base64 Data URLs in DefinitionJSON)

story-context.summary: Replace embedded base64 Data URL backgrounds in form definitions with persisted background assets. Introduce an asset persistence model (DB + storage provider abstraction) and ensure builder preview and public renderer resolve background assets consistently. All upload/runtime limits must be configuration-backed via config.AppSetting (loaded by ConfigurationService).
story-context.problem-statement: Background images embedded as base64 Data URLs bloat FormVersion.DefinitionJSON, slow saves/loads, inflate version history, and prevent lifecycle controls (limits, dedupe, deletion, and storage provider swaps). Epic 5 must make the builder production-ready before delivering preview/production and publish governance.

key-features.feature: Form definition stores background image as asset reference (no embedded base64/Data URLs)
Backend asset persistence model (tenant-scoped metadata + binary storage) with lifecycle fields
Storage provider abstraction (Local dev → Azure Blob prod) swappable via configuration
Config-backed limits enforced via config.AppSetting and ConfigurationService (no hard-coded limits)
Builder + renderer parity plan for resolving assets consistently (avoid absolute hostnames)
Defensive guard against embedded Data URLs (no migration expected, but block/sanitize payloads)

reference-documents.document: Story scope, acceptance criteria, and proposed AppSetting keys
Epic 5 anchors: Preview & Testing System (4A) and Form Publishing & Hosting (7); publish request flow (deferred for Story 5.5+)
Architecture contract (camelCase API responses; resolver parity; avoid per-feature casing fallbacks)

technical-context.technology: Azure Blob Storage provider (prod; deferred validation in dev)

key-types.type: A minimal reference stored in the form definition (e.g., assetId + placement metadata). No bytes.
Tenant-scoped DB record containing metadata (mime, size, dimensions, sha256) and storage locator (provider + key).
Runtime component that converts an asset reference into a usable URL/stream for builder preview and public renderer.

key-files.file: Replace background handling to store asset references and placement (no base64 Data URLs)
Resolve background assets via a shared/runtime resolver path
Add asset upload/list/resolve endpoints and persistence service(s)
Ensure required AppSetting keys are retrievable via ConfigurationService
Asset schemas/service/storage abstraction (exact file names finalized during decomposition)

done-criteria.criterion: Background images are referenced by assetId (no base64/Data URLs in DefinitionJSON)
Asset upload creates persisted metadata + stored binary in configured provider
Builder preview and public renderer both render backgrounds reliably for the same form version
Limits are enforced using config.AppSetting values (via ConfigurationService)
Defensive guard exists for embedded Data URLs

acceptance-criteria.criterion: Saving a form with a background does not persist any data:image/* Data URL in DefinitionJSON
Asset records are tenant-scoped and include mime, size, dimensions, and storage locator
Upload rejects files that violate size/mime/dimension limits based on AppSetting values
Storage provider selection is config-based and does not require schema/definition redesign
Asset resolution avoids persisting absolute hostnames (supports future custom domains)
Embedded Data URL payloads are blocked or stripped deterministically with clear error/warning

forbidden-zones.zone: Do not introduce preview/production governance, publish requests, or admin review workflow (deferred to Story 5.5+)
Do not introduce company-level defaults/brand inheritance (deferred to Story 5.2)
Do not introduce schema/validation alignment work beyond the Data URL guard (deferred to Story 5.3)
Do not hard-code upload/runtime limits; all must be config-backed via config.AppSetting

out-of-scope.item: Governance workflow: preview/production + publish request + admin review (Story 5.5+)

risks.risk: Asset access control must remain correct across authenticated builder and token-gated public renderer.
Implementing provider swap incorrectly can couple the schema to a single storage backend; keep provider abstraction strict.
Large images can impact rendering performance; enforce AppSetting limits and prefer efficient formats.
